caption_used: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive Reasoning. The Categorical pie chart comprises four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%), Negation (27.91%), Limiter (27.91%), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%). In the Approximate Number Generation chart, Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%, followed by Approximate Quantities at 33.26% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart shows a near-even split, with Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%.
model_annotation:
The “Categorical” pie chart represents the distribution of four categorical quantifier/operation types across a whole, shown as 4 slices with labels and percentage values printed inside each segment and no separate legend; the slices are Universal Quantifiers (light gray-blue) at 29.07%, Negation (light peach/orange) at 27.91%, Limiter (light pink) at 27.91%, and Existential Quantifiers (pale green) at 15.12%, with no slice visually offset or exploded and the segments arranged around the circle without an explicit descending-size order.

The “Approximate Number Generation” pie chart represents the distribution of three operation types for approximate number generation, shown as 3 slices with internal text labels and percentages and no legend; the segments are Approximate Quantities (very pale yellow/cream) at 45.03%, Comparative Relationships (light blue) at 36.26%, and Absolute Absence (light lavender/purple) at 18.71%, with none of the slices emphasized via separation and the wedges placed around the circle without a clearly indicated ordering rule.

The “Disjunctive & Conjunctive” pie chart depicts the split between two logical operation categories, shown as 2 slices with labels and percentages printed within each half and no legend; the Disjunctive slice (very light blue-gray) is 49.51% and the Conjunctive slice (light mauve/purple) is 50.49%, with a simple two-part division and no visual emphasis such as exploded wedges.
